## Overview
Tests sex differences across 14 attention and resilience variables using Mann-Whitney U tests with Benjamini-Hochberg correction. Effect sizes are reported as rank-biserial correlations and plotted as a forest plot. Also reruns the attention-resilience correlations separately for male and female participants, and computes partial Spearman correlations controlling for sex.

```{r}
#now i want to analyze differences in gender

data$sex <- factor(data$sex,
                   levels = c(0, 1),
                   labels = c("Male", "Female"))
wilcox.test(cdrisc ~ sex, data = data) #male cd risc vs female cd risc
wilcox.test(d_prime ~ sex, data = data) #male d' vs female d'

variables <- c(
  "meanrt",
  "stdrt",
  "err_com",
  "err_om",
  "imp_err3",
  "imp_err_total",
  "d_prime",
  "dsm_inatten",
  "bis_first",
  "bis_second",
  "cdrisc",
  "cyrm_total",
  "cyrm_personal",
  "cyrm_care"
)

gender_results <- data.frame()

for (v in variables) {

  temp <- data[, c("sex", v)]
  temp <- temp[complete.cases(temp), ]

  test <- wilcox.test(temp[[v]] ~ temp$sex) #running Mann Whitney

  gender_results <- rbind(
    gender_results,
    data.frame(
      Variable = v,
      W = test$statistic, #W is the rank sum stat, not interp by itself
      P = test$p.value
    )
  )
}

# BH correction
gender_results$P_BH <- p.adjust(gender_results$P, method = "BH") #another BH correction

# Round
gender_results$P <- round(gender_results$P, 4)
gender_results$P_BH <- round(gender_results$P_BH, 4)

# Significance
gender_results$Sig <- ifelse(gender_results$P_BH < .001, "***",
                      ifelse(gender_results$P_BH < .01, "**",
                      ifelse(gender_results$P_BH < .05, "*", "")))

View(gender_results)

write.csv(
  gender_results,
  "~/Desktop/research/Elton/SARA/Gender_Differences.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

#non parametric, using medians instead of means when the data isn't distributed
```

```{r}
# better version with effect size looped in

gender_results <- data.frame()

for (v in variables) {

  temp <- data[, c("sex", v)]
  temp <- temp[complete.cases(temp), ]

  test <- wilcox.test(temp[[v]] ~ temp$sex)

  n1 <- sum(temp$sex == "Male")
  n2 <- sum(temp$sex == "Female")
  U <- as.numeric(test$statistic)

  rank_biserial <- (2 * U) / (n1 * n2) - 1 #converts W stat into effect size - tells you how large the difference is (larger the more different)
#positive = males have higher values, negative = femail have higher values
  
  gender_results <- rbind(
    gender_results,
    data.frame(
      Variable = v,
      N_Male = n1,
      N_Female = n2,
      W = U,
      Rank_Biserial = round(rank_biserial, 3),
      P = test$p.value
    )
  )
}

gender_results$P_BH <- p.adjust(gender_results$P, method = "BH")
gender_results

write.csv(
  gender_results,
  "~/Desktop/research/Elton/SARA/Gender_Differences_again.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#going to make a forest plot!!!
library(ggplot2)

# Keep only significant variables
sig_gender <- subset(
  gender_results,
  Variable %in% c("meanrt", "stdrt", "err_com", "cdrisc")
)

# Nice labels
sig_gender$Variable <- factor(
  sig_gender$Variable,
  levels = c("cdrisc", "err_com", "stdrt", "meanrt"),
  labels = c(
    "CD-RISC",
    "Commission Errors",
    "RT Variability",
    "Mean RT"
  )
)

ggplot(sig_gender,
       aes(x = Rank_Biserial,
           y = Variable)) +

  # zero line
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "gray50"
  ) +

  # connect points to zero
  geom_segment(
    aes(x = 0,
        xend = Rank_Biserial,
        y = Variable,
        yend = Variable),
    color = "gray75",
    linewidth = 1
  ) +

  # points
  geom_point(
    color = "#FA4616",
    size = 5
  ) +

  # effect size labels
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", Rank_Biserial)),
    nudge_x = 0.025,
    size = 5,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Significant Gender Differences",
    subtitle = "Rank-biserial effect sizes",
    x = "Female Higher                     Rank-Biserial Correlation                     Male Higher",
    y = NULL
  ) +

  theme_classic(base_size = 15) +

  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    axis.line.y = element_blank()
  )
ggsave(
  "~/Desktop/research/Elton/SARA/Gender_Effect_Size_Plot.pdf",
  width = 8,
  height = 5
)
```

```{r}

data <- read.csv(
  "~/Desktop/research/Elton/SARA/sara_data_VM.csv",
  na.strings = "-999"
)

table(data$sex)

males <- subset(data, sex == 0)
females <- subset(data, sex == 1)

nrow(males)
nrow(females)

attention <- c(
  "meanrt",
  "stdrt",
  "err_com",
  "err_om",
  "imp_err3",
  "imp_err_total",
  "d_prime",
  "dsm_inatten",
  "bis_first",
  "bis_second"
)

resilience <- c(
  "cdrisc",
  "cyrm_total",
  "cyrm_personal",
  "cyrm_care"
)

run_correlations <- function(df) {

  results <- data.frame()

  for(att in attention){

    for(res in resilience){

      temp <- df[, c(att, res)]
      temp <- temp[complete.cases(temp), ]

      test <- cor.test(
        temp[[att]],
        temp[[res]],
        method = "spearman",
        exact = FALSE
      )

      results <- rbind(
        results,
        data.frame(
          Attention = att,
          Resilience = res,
          N = nrow(temp),
          Rho = round(unname(test$estimate), 3),
          P = test$p.value
        )
      )
    }
  }

  results$P_BH <- p.adjust(results$P, method = "BH")

  results$Sig <- ifelse(results$P_BH < .001, "***",
                 ifelse(results$P_BH < .01, "**",
                 ifelse(results$P_BH < .05, "*", "")))

  results <- results[order(results$P_BH), ]

  return(results)
}

male_results <- run_correlations(males)

female_results <- run_correlations(females)

print(male_results)

print(female_results)

write.csv(
  male_results,
  "~/Desktop/research/Elton/SARA/Male_Correlations.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  female_results,
  "~/Desktop/research/Elton/SARA/Female_Correlations.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#controlling for sex
install.packages("ppcor")
```

```{r}
library(ppcor)

data$sex_num <- ifelse(data$sex == "Female", 1, 0)

partial_results <- data.frame()

for(att in attention){

  for(res in resilience){

    temp <- data[, c(att, res, "sex_num")]
    temp <- temp[complete.cases(temp), ]

    test <- pcor.test(
      x = temp[[att]],
      y = temp[[res]],
      z = temp$sex_num,
      method = "spearman"
    )

    partial_results <- rbind(
      partial_results,
      data.frame(
        Attention = att,
        Resilience = res,
        N = nrow(temp),
        Partial_Rho = round(test$estimate, 3),
        P = test$p.value
      )
    )
  }
}

partial_results$P_BH <- p.adjust(partial_results$P, method = "BH")

partial_results$Sig <- ifelse(
  partial_results$P_BH < .001, "***",
  ifelse(
    partial_results$P_BH < .01, "**",
    ifelse(partial_results$P_BH < .05, "*", "")
  )
)

partial_results <- partial_results[order(partial_results$P_BH), ]

write.csv(
  partial_results,
  "~/Desktop/research/Elton/SARA/Partial_Correlations_Controlling_for_Sex.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```
